summary: Roadmap item 6 of dimension32-global-topology: how A_5 partner spheres specialize across the 33 closure incidences 8 -> 12, 12 -> 16 and 8 -> 16, as closed kernel Gauss-graph fibers with two-sided real certificates and attaching maps, run as a Codex program.

reconciliation.note: Steps reconciled on 2026-11-20 against ledger rows 1 to 2w and the README; the program file's orchestrator note after 2w states each step's evidence and remainder.

scope: Evidence bundle docs/evidence/a5-kernel-attachments (scripts, records, README, ledger) and the program file docs/design/a5-kernel-attachments-program.md; the 33 incidences between the nullity-8, nullity-12 and nullity-16 orbits. Same-nullity incidences are recorded once by the constant-rank lemma. Nullity 4 and roadmap items 7-8 proper stay out of scope.
next_action: Sub-step 3a holds (ledger row 3a); next, the variation of the attaching datum along the boundary orbit and the seven higher-order rows of 2c.

steps.action: Enumerate all 33 incidences with exact boundary points, moved points included, and decide per incidence whether the first-order effective form on the boundary kernel is complex-linear in the normal direction.
steps.acceptance: Fails if a declared incidence lacks an exact verified point or a second boundary point reverses a complex-linearity verdict without explanation.

receipts.result: The closure order gives 33 incidences (15 at 8 to 12, 8 at 12 to 16, 10 at 8 to 16); all 21 canonical, unipotently moved and boost-moved boundary points pass their orbit, source-closure, nullity, frame and first-order checks, and partner purity extends the complex-linearity verdict to every boundary point at first order.

steps.action: Compute the closed Gauss-graph fiber in Gr(4,6) for every 8 -> 12 incidence with an exact upper bound and filling exact real arcs, and its variation over the boundary moduli.
steps.acceptance: Fails if an exact arc limit escapes the upper bound, a point of the bound is reached by no certified arc, or a moved boundary point changes the set beyond the stated variation.
steps.reason: Ledger rows 2i (eight) and 2j-c (six) compute 14 of 15 fibers at the selected basepoints, each equal to the real limit set on the slice germ by row 2l; E8-bar to VB imports its fiber (row 2q; A5-005, open in characteristic 0 by A5-315). Open: the E8-bar to VB real limit set, the variation along the boundary orbit beyond the sampled boost (rows 2r, 2w), and arcs leaving the slice on V and VB.

steps.action: The same for the 8 incidences 12 -> 16 and the 10 incidences 8 -> 16, starting with a two-approach path-dependence test.
steps.acceptance: Fails on the same criteria as the 8 -> 12 step.
steps.reason: Rows 2k-c and 2m give eight fibers and real limit sets; row 2q imports the ten 8-to-16 fibers and row 2t with the README decides their real limit sets as point sets (X: A5-270, A5-305; Iso: A5-446; W8: A5-448; E8-bar conditional, A5-425). Open: the header-slice characteristic-0 fibers (A5-293, A5-346), the non-reduced E8-bar scheme on the header slice (A5-449, A5-559), and the header-to-weight-slice coordinate identification (A5-583).

steps.action: Compare limits composed through nullity 12 with the direct 8 -> 16 limit sets.
steps.acceptance: Fails if a composed limit lies outside the direct limit set or the reverse inclusion is claimed without arcs.
steps.reason: Row 2s: 41 chains and 136 sections; a composed limit lies in a linear section of the direct fiber. Open: the hypothesis that through VB the composed limit set is the reduced section (needs a flat family over VB), and which planes of a section through B9 or V are composed limits.

steps.action: Describe the link-to-limit-set maps and the sphere-union maps into the boundary partner sphere with their homotopy data in a form a global model can assemble.
steps.acceptance: Fails if a stated homotopy datum is neither computed by a replayed producer nor labeled as an argument.
